> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 43 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **153** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e63819307b55416f3323009937eaee1e2e4847b5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aff791908fb188fb034c68d98c6e78971bf78438` — the merge of head `b563cd4c44db27b6092ffb35ac1921abc4695f9a` into base `e63819307b55416f3323009937eaee1e2e4847b5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aff791908fb188fb034c68d98c6e78971bf78438 && git checkout aff791908fb188fb034c68d98c6e78971bf78438
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e63819307b55416f3323009937eaee1e2e4847b5 b563cd4c44db27b6092ffb35ac1921abc4695f9a && git checkout -B drift-repro e63819307b55416f3323009937eaee1e2e4847b5 && git merge --no-ff b563cd4c44db27b6092ffb35ac1921abc4695f9a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e63819307b55416f3323009937eaee1e2e4847b5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e63819307b55416f3323009937eaee1e2e4847b5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b563cd4c44db27b6092ffb35ac1921abc4695f9a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate-catalog.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-own-name-set.posture.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegable-scope-no-identity-positions.posture.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-permission-zoo.dogfood.test.ts + packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (`mapDataError` / `classifyDataError`), packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts (`resolveThrownHttpError`), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (the `isPermissionDeniedError` catch and `errorFromThrown`), packages/rest/src/security-routes.ts (the explain route's 403 arm), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/invitation-placement.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts (`beforeCreateInvitation`), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (the standard catalog), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs; prose faces read but not judged as code: .changeset/26189-delegation-scope-violation-code.md, content/docs/references/api/{automation-api,contract,error-code-ledger}.mdx. Inputs: card #26189 body and all three comments (triage 6420690630, claim 6423979372, os-dev-report 6427138182), ruling 6416233738 and item reading 6415971852 on #26059, PR #26320 body, file list and the net diff `origin/main...origin/pr-26320` (16 files, +357/-29), and the 41 check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

Read against the ruling's test (6416233738 Q3 child 3, item reading 6415971852 item 3): a reason that describes the caller's OWN delegated scope may take the new code; everything else keeps `PERMISSION_DENIED`; ruling #24914 B′ (an ordinary `PERMISSION_DENIED` stays opaque) is unchanged.

**1. The accept set is unchanged. Right.** Every hunk in `delegated-admin-gate.ts` changes the class thrown, never the predicate: `outsideScope(...)` wraps five existing reason strings, `firstApprovalFailure` keeps the wrap through the `(scope from 'SET')` suffix, and `refusalFor` picks the class by `typeof failure === 'string'`. No admission flips and no refusal flips; the thrown values differ only in `code`, `name` and the message prefix. The ten `PERMISSION_DENIED` control cells in the new `[#26189]` block and the dogfood CONTROL (an unanchored assignment at the real `/data` door) pin the non-scope side.

**2. Which refusals move, judged one by one. Right, and every moved reason is about the caller's own scope.**
- Moved (5 sites): `assertAssignmentWrite` new-row unit outside the subtree (`:1154`), pre-image unit outside the subtree (`:1161`), position distributing a set off the allowlist (`:1167`); `assertDirectGrantWrite` set off the allowlist (`:1198`), target user outside the subtree (`:1204`). Each is exactly one of the three reasons the ruling names (unit outside the subtree, set not in the allowlist, target user outside the subtree). Each message names only what the caller supplied (a unit id, a position or set name, a user id) and the verdict "outside / not in" relative to the caller's own scope. Safe to show.
- Kept `PERMISSION_DENIED` (every other throw): the audience anchor (`:422`), principal-less (`:434`), `sys_member` tenant-only (`:465`), organization boundary (`:499`), plain CRUD without a scope (`:506`), filter writes (`:522`), every `assertSelfDelegation` `deny` (`:981`, ADR-0091 D3), `manageAssignments` absent, unanchored new row or pre-image, `assertScopeGrantContainment` (`:1246`, a plain string), the direct-grant catalog miss (`unresolved`), no target user, target user with no business unit. These are the card's note (entry refusals that are not about the caller's delegated scope) plus the per-scope reasons the ruling does not list. The PR body's per-throw-site table matches the code on this head line for line.

**3. No hidden-reason refusal leaks through the new code.** The new class is reachable only through `refusalFor`, and `refusalFor` answers it only for a `ScopeViolation`, which only `outsideScope(...)` builds, at the five sites above. No other producer can mint `DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION` (the class is not exported from `plugin-security/src/index.ts`; `PermissionDeniedError` and `isPermissionDeniedError` still are). The `details` the gate attaches (`operation`, `object`, `position` or `permissionSet`, all caller input) do not reach the wire at either door: `resolveThrownHttpError` builds `details` only from a non-string `code`, `issues` and validation `fields`, and `mapDataError`'s passthrough carries the same resolver's answer. B′ holds: every `PERMISSION_DENIED` on the platform is byte-identical on the wire.

**4. The message prefix and the four consumers. Right.** The new message opens `[Security] Outside your delegated scope: ...`, so the three-limb matcher (code `PERMISSION_DENIED`, name `PermissionDeniedError`, prefix `[Security] Access denied`) misses it everywhere it is read:
- `mapDataError` (`data-error-classification.ts:1406–1417`): no bespoke arm knows the class, the 403 arm misses on all three limbs, and the declared-status passthrough answers `403` with the registered code and the thrown message; pinned per cell by `expectScopeViolation` (`wire.body.code`, `wire.body.error`) and at the real door by the two flipped dogfood pins. The ablation in the PR (prefix restored, both door pins red, control green) is the right experiment for this claim.
- `isPermissionDeniedError` (`errors.ts:408–414`): `false` for the new class, pinned per cell. Its one runtime caller, `http-dispatcher.ts:3106`, therefore skips the `PERMISSION_DENIED` catch and the throw falls to `errorFromThrown` → `resolveThrownHttpError`, which reads `status` 403 and the now-registered code and keeps it as `code` (not demoted to `declaredCode`, because the ledger row exists on this same head). The posture test on the dispatcher door pins `[403, 'DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION']`.
- `security-routes.ts:255–260` (the explain route): same three limbs, so it would miss too; but the dev's reading is right that the route cannot receive this throw at all: `security-plugin-explain-access.ts:149–154` calls `scopesCoverUser(...)` (which never throws the gate's refusal) under a catch that answers false (`.catch`, arrow to `false`) and never `assert`. The predicate-level pin (name, code, prefix) is the right strength for an unreachable door.
- plugin-auth `isInvitationPlacementGateRefusal` (`auth-manager.ts:1401–1405`): the invitation placement dry-run (`invitation-placement.ts:168`) calls `gate.assert` on a `sys_user_position` insert, so `assertAssignmentWrite`'s unit-outside-subtree and set-off-allowlist reasons DO reach it as the new class; without the one-line widening `beforeCreateInvitation` (`auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts:393`) would have answered the `503` read-fault. With it the answer stays `403 INVITE_PLACEMENT_OUTSIDE_ISSUER_SCOPE` with the gate's message, as before; pinned red-first in `auth-manager.test.ts`. Required, not defensive.
- The other in-repo readers of `code === 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` were walked and none can receive this gate's throw: objectql `isReadRefusal` (a `sys_file` sub-read), plugin-auth's `last-admin-guard` / `objectql-adapter` / actor guards (their own guards' throws), `verify/parent-write-reach.ts` (CBP master reads), the dogfood anonymous-door sweep (principal-less, which stays `PERMISSION_DENIED`).

**5. The ledger row. Well formed and not a synonym.** SCREAMING_SNAKE, appended once under `@objectstack/plugin-security` (the stamping package, so the provenance gate's "stamping package lists it" rule is met by construction; no `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` entry needed), with the trailing comment stating status, condition, and why it is its own meaning. `standardSynonymOf`: not an HTTP reason phrase; the token prong needs every token in one standard member and `DELEGATION`, `SCOPE`, `VIOLATION` appear in no member of `StandardErrorCode` (`errors.zod.ts`), so it answers `undefined`; no `STANDARD_SYNONYM_WAIVERS` entry, correctly (the `FORBIDDEN` → `PERMISSION_DENIED` waiver is the shape this code must not take, and does not). The new test cell pins parse, provenance row, `standardSynonymOf` undefined, and no waiver. The regenerated docs carry the member in sorted position and the `+345 → +346` count moves in `contract.mdx` and `automation-api.mdx` alike.

**6. The dev's open question (`manageAssignments` absent and adminScope containment stay `PERMISSION_DENIED`). Option A is right under the ruling.** The ruling and the card's acceptance name three reasons; "every other refusal of the gate ... is unchanged on the wire" is the card's own acceptance line. Both kept reasons do describe the caller's own grant, so B is defensible on the safety test alone, but moving them is a widening of the ruled list, and the card says a question born in a child goes on the child linking the parent, not into the diff. Left for the seat in ③.

**7. Multi-scope semantics.** With several held scopes the surfaced reason is still "first failure of the last scope tried" and the code follows that reason, so a caller whose last scope fails on a non-scope reason answers `PERMISSION_DENIED` even when an earlier scope failed on a scope reason. That is the pre-existing ordering, unchanged, and never shows a hidden reason; noted, not a defect.

### ② Semver level

- Changesets: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/plugin-security` patch, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch. Right: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no authorable key, value or type moves), and AGENTS.md's rule is "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `@objectstack/types` is touched only by a test import; dogfood is unpublished. No changeset is owed for either.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening: ...)` on the PR body and the changeset. Right, and the dev's correction of the claim's `no` is the ledger's own header: "Registering a code widens this face and is therefore a Clause-② change, door or no door". The status and the accept set do not narrow, so `(narrowing)` would be wrong.
- `**BREAKING** (a wire-answer change), shipped as patch` plus the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: consistent with each other and with the gate (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads the banner and the `!` as breaking signals and then requires exactly one marker; `no-migration-prescription` is a documented category, and the why-text closes the other categories on facts). The precedent shape in `plugin-security/CHANGELOG.md` ("BREAKING for a caller that relied on such a write landing. A non-protocol change, shipped as patch") is the same class. Check-run `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- The `!` in the PR title (`feat(plugin-security,spec,plugin-auth)!:`) matches the banner, and it is what made the full dogfood run (297 files / 2528 tests, 0 failed, per the report).
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success). This is a schema-face review, not a landing record for a governed path.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Clause-② deviation (claim `no`, measured `yes (widening)`).** Answered: the dev is right and the claim was wrong; the changeset and PR body carry the correct line. No action.
2. **File surface beyond the claim** (`showcase-permission-zoo.dogfood.test.ts`, three posture/catalog tests, `errors.test.ts`, the three generated `.mdx`): all are pins flipped by the ruled change or `gen:docs` output of the ledger row; no second `packages/spec/**` change. Answered, in scope.
3. **`security-routes.ts` pinned at predicate level only.** Answered in ①.4: the explain door cannot receive the throw, so the predicate pin is the honest strength; a route-level pin would assert an unreachable path.
4. **`DelegationScopeViolationError` not exported from the plugin index.** Accepted: clients and the two doors read `code`, and plugin-auth deliberately reads it structurally. If a host plugin later needs `instanceof`, that is a one-line export with no wire change.
5. **The "request review" step skipped (no MCP write).** A process note for the seat, not a contract finding.
6. **Open question A/B.** Answered in ①.6: A stands; if the seat wants B it is a ruling question on #26059 (anchored there per the ruling's last line), carried as a follow-up card, never a rider on this PR.
7. **Out-of-scope finding (console `isPermissionError` treats any 403 as the fixed line).** Correctly carried by #26190 (child 4, `Blocked-by:` this card); nothing here changes the console until it lands.
8. **One observation for child 4 (#26190), not a defect here.** The pre-image reason ("the existing assignment's business unit 'X' is outside the delegated subtree") names the business unit of a row the caller addressed by id and may not be able to read. It is within the ruling's "unit outside the subtree" and the wire already carried that sentence verbatim under `PERMISSION_DENIED` at both doors before this PR, so nothing new reaches the network; what changes is that the console will render it once #26190 lands. The UI seat should know this is the one scope-violation message that names another row's data rather than the caller's own input.
9. **Check-runs on the head.** Concluded success: Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate), Check Changeset, Check PR Size, single-writer-path guard, Governed Surface Queue Guard, issue-claim guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, card-claims-branch guard, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, filter, Flag docs affected, Spec property liveness, Part-of guard, Check Documentation Links. Skipped by path filter or opt-in: Temporal Conformance, Dogfood shards 1–3, Dogfood Verify CLI, 18.x harness, packed-tarball smoke. Not yet concluded at review time (in_progress): Test Core 1/8–8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Type Check · source gates / debt ledger / consumer gates / workspace, Lint · repo & tooling gates / docs & code guards / ESLint / CI, release & engine gates / scoped · query-options erasure / scoped · slot lookup & corpus. The verdict below is on the diff and the cited code; the owning seat lands only once the eight required contexts are green (AGENTS.md §7), and a red there is read against the dev's local readings before any re-run.
